content.text: {"headline":"Approve P1: switch on IVR callback for the evening dip (general 18:00-20:00, payments 18:30-20:00) at no extra cost.","why":"Both queues are short because of a sick wave. Payments has 15 absences against a usual 2.8, and general has 13 against 2.6, mostly agents who went home unwell after lunch. Call volume is close to forecast, so this is a staffing gap, not a demand spike. Service level has dropped to 49% on payments and 61.6% on general. Even so, the forecast for the disruption window (15:30-19:45) is that service level recovers above the 80% target without intervention: 89.2% with no action. P1 is the cheapest plan that meets target. It lifts the window to 89.6% (89.6% on both queues) and trims abandons from 2.6% to 2.4%, costs ₹0 and has no policy issues. Rest of day stays at 87.9%.","trade_offs":["P1's gain over doing nothing is small (+0.4 points, 0.2 points fewer abandons). Its main value is giving customers a callback option during the evening at no cost.","P3 (chat deflection, callback and light overtime) reaches 94.4% in the window, 93.6% for the rest of day and 1.5% abandons, for ₹1,632. That is more headroom if absences keep rising.","P4 gives the strongest result (94.9% window, 1.3% abandons) at ₹3,252. P2's overtime-only plan costs ₹2,520 but is weaker than P3.","Both queues stay balanced under P1 (89.6% each), so neither queue is protected at the other's expense."],"watch":"Payments is the queue to watch: it is furthest behind right now (49%) and has the higher absence count. If more agents go home, or payments service level is still not recovering by about 17:00, move to P3 for ₹1,632. No escalation to the duty manager is needed."}
